name: Kalakand
ingredients: Full-fat milk (1 gallon / 4 liters), preferably from grass-fed cows
Lemon juice (4 tbsp), freshly squeezed to curdle the milk
Ghee (3 tbsp), best quality or home-clarified butter
Green cardamom pods (8-10), seeds crushed to a powder
Saffron strands (a generous pinch), steeped in 2 tbsp warm milk
Slivered pistachios (2 tbsp), preferably from Kashmir
Rose water (1 tsp), natural and food-grade
instructions: 1. In a heavy-bottomed pan, bring milk to a rolling boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent scorching. 2. Reduce heat to low and slowly add lemon juice while stirring until milk curdles and whey separates. Remove from heat. 3. Drain the curdled milk through a cheesecloth-lined colander, rinse with cold water to remove lemon flavor, and tie the cloth to hang for 30 minutes to drain excess whey. 4. In the same pan, melt ghee over medium heat. Crumble the hung chenna (solidified milk solids) into the pan and cook, stirring continuously, for 5 minutes until it releases moisture and turns paste-like. 5. Add sugar and continue stirring over low-medium heat for 10-12 minutes until the mixture thickens, leaves the sides of the pan, and forms a soft, cohesive mass. 6. Remove from heat. Mix in cardamom powder, saffron milk, rose water, and half of the slivered nuts. 7. Transfer the mixture onto a greased plate or tray, spread evenly to 1-inch thickness, and garnish with remaining nuts. Press gently to set. 8. Let it cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for 2 hours. Cut into squares or diamond shapes and serve at room temperature or chilled.
description: A creamy, cardamom-kissed jewel of solidified sweet milk, embodying the pastoral abundance of Punjab.
